name: assembly-qualification-is-stripped
why: A .NET publisher reaching for typeof(T).AssemblyQualifiedName gets all of this. Without the strip the subject changes on every assembly version bump, so a routine release would silently register a new subject and orphan the old contract. DESIGN §3 enumerates assembly, version, culture and public-key-token; all four sit after the first comma, so one rule covers the list and there is nothing for another SDK to get subtly wrong.
